method: Four original PNG opens at original detail, before reading author reports, specs, or modern previews. No crops, reopens, or other image reads.

inventory: One solid skew quadrilateral frame: upper horizontal edge through A, right oblique side, lower horizontal edge through C and B, and left oblique side. It depicts a second plane/frame, not an instructional grid.
One oval plane labeled alpha below/left. Its lower/front and lateral contour is solid; its upper/back contour is dashed, including the upper-right curved section.
A is above the lower plane, on the frame's upper edge. C is the lower endpoint of solid AC and is left of B. B is the lower endpoint of solid AB, on the same lower frame line as C.

Solid AC slopes slightly right downward; solid AB slopes substantially right downward. The visible A junction is dark/point-like; B has a dark endpoint junction; C has a thick line junction. Do not infer an additional standalone point from thick scan strokes.

Line m slopes from lower-left/front upward-right/back. Its exposed extension below the plane/front intersection is solid, and the continuation in the oval is dashed. It crosses the C-B carrier to the right of B.
An explicit small right-angle glyph is at the crossing of m with the C-B carrier, left/below that crossing. There is no separately printed right-angle glyph at C or B.

The solid frame carrier extends left of C and right of B. Its intersections with the oval contour are unlabeled. AB crosses the dashed back contour and AC meets/crosses it in projection, without extra labels or point dots.
No arrowheads, coordinate axes, grid cells, values, units, equality ticks, or added labels are printed.
figures.spatialCaution: A line-line right-angle marker is a spatial claim; a perspective plane drawing need not show every spatial perpendicular as a screen right angle. Unmarked screen crossings with plane contours are not new spatial points.

inventory: One complete solid oval plane boundary labeled alpha in the lower-left interior. There is no dashed/hidden back contour.
A is above the plane. C is below A, and B is to the right of C inside the plane.

Three solid directed strokes: A to C downward with arrowhead at C; A to B downward-right with arrowhead at B; C to B rightward with arrowhead at B. These are directions/vectors, not three undirected segments.
A-C and A-B cross the upper oval boundary only in the projection; those boundary crossings are unlabeled and have no independent point dots.

A separate solid oblique line m rises from the lower/front oval boundary toward its upper-right boundary. A labeled dark dot M lies on it in the lower-right interior. The arrow points up/right toward N, whose label is farther up/right near the arrow. The lower exposed part is labeled m.
The m carrier and the directed C-B stroke are separate in the picture, with no printed shared point.
A, B, and C have thick directed-line endpoints/junctions; M is an explicit standalone dark marker on m. N is a label at the upper directed portion, with no distinct round dot evident in the source.
No right-angle squares, equality ticks, metric values, axes, instructional grids, extra labels, or dashed strokes are printed.
figures.spatialCaution: The arrows and vector endpoints carry meaning. The source does not require the drawn plane boundary to intersect A-C or A-B as a geometric curve in three-space.

inventory: One base quadrilateral: A upper-left/back, B lower-left/front, C lower-right/front, D upper-right/back. Its four solid edges are AB, BC, CD, and DA.
M is above A. Four solid apex-to-base strokes are MA, MB, MC, and MD. MA is nearly vertical, MB slopes down/left, MC slopes down/right, and MD slopes more shallowly down/right.
MA and AB are visibly heavier than some other scan strokes; all eight edges remain solid rather than dashed. No explicit arrowheads or equal-length ticks are shown.
M is a dark point-like apex. A is a dark three-edge junction; B, C, and D are endpoint/junction vertices. No other labeled or standalone points occur.

The drawn MC crosses AD at an unlabeled location. No dot, label, break, or right-angle glyph is printed there: it is a projection-only crossing, not a sixth vertex or an incidence in the spatial solid.
The labels M, A, B, C, D are outside/adjacent to their respective vertices. No alpha label, plane frame, axis, instructional grid, dimensions, units, right-angle squares, or other annotations occur.
figures.spatialCaution: A screen quadrilateral and apex are a projection of a spatial figure. Spatial base shape, perpendicularity, and equal-length claims must be checked against edition prose and a three-dimensional model, not screen slopes or screen distances.

inventory: One triangle with A at the left end of a horizontal base AB, B at the right end, and C above/right of A. Its three sides AB, AC, and CB are solid.
One separate solid vertical-looking stroke NM: N is a dark dot above the triangle and M is a dark dot inside its projected outline. N is directly above M in the source projection.
NM crosses AC at an unlabeled location above M. No dot, label, right-angle square, or break is printed at that crossing; it is projection-only and is not M.
There are no drawn segments MA, MB, MC, NA, NB, or NC. The only non-triangle stroke is NM.
A, B, and C are solid side junctions, without separate round markers clearly distinguished from stroke endpoints. M and N are explicit round dark markers.

Labels A, B, C, M, N are printed next to their respective endpoints/vertices. No plane label, arrows, dashed strokes, equality ticks, dimensions, axes, instructional grids, circle, angle arcs, or right-angle squares occur.
figures.spatialCaution: NM can be perpendicular to the triangle's spatial plane without being perpendicular to AC in the two-dimensional image. The unmarked AC/NM crossing must not acquire a point label or spatial incidence.
